## Why it works

The comments thank it for being short and clear, and add what it left out. The most-liked viewer comment is the missing safety step: "Another tip: always shut down the circuit when wiring outlets and switches. Then, record the circuit number on the back of the plate cover with a sharpie" (764 likes); the next adds an order of work: "start at ground, then neutral, then hot. And reverse for dismantling outlets" (480 likes). The thanks are about value and tone: "Most pros would charge a few hundred bucks for what you give away for free. Thanks for being the neighbor I wish I had." (266 likes), and even an apprentice learned from the strip gauge: "I was totally not aware of that little measuring guide on the back of the outlet" (50 likes). A regular viewer names the pace: "Love that they are short and to the point." (8 likes). The opening states the count and the bonus in 10 seconds and the first mistake lands straight after; then a new ranked mistake every 30 to 50 seconds, each with a one-line reason, at about 248 words a minute, the fastest delivery in the library. The held-back bonus works as the reason to stay past the halfway mark, and it pays with a product upgrade the viewer can buy and use the same day. What viewers did after is mostly adding to it: the top comments are viewers handing on their own tips (power off and label the plate, ground first, a ground-wire wrap), which is the reaction a short, confident list gets. The channel's pinned comment links the clamp outlet, the tester and the stripper.
